constitutional_rules.statement: One globally ordered cyclic sushi track carries both normal cards and commodity cards.
Only the closed normal_card and commodity_card kinds are mixed on the unified track.
Separate tracks and region-bound ordinary-card pools are not V0.7 authorities.
Every track card has one primary identity from the closed six-color set.
A viewer sees and may claim concrete cards only in that viewer's exclusive local segment.
Cards enter nearest the hidden lead and pass local segments in the frozen hidden lead order.
Both card kinds share order, movement, and color distribution while the kind ratio remains independently balanced.
Sharing a track does not merge normal-card and commodity inventory ownership.
Every color cycle is recalculated from a uniform six-color baseline without inheritance or compounding.
GDP does not change unified-track color or card-kind supply.
Each player precommits one increase color and one different decrease color for the next cycle.
Revealed directions are public while weights, lead identity, and raw contribution decomposition remain secret.
The boundary lead has double the normal player's symmetric increase/decrease influence.
Players prepare the next stance during active play and all legal stances reveal at the boundary without a waiting phase.
A missing or illegal stance contributes no increase or decrease.
One hidden order is generated authoritatively and remains fixed for the match.
Every player leads exactly once per macro round and each following round reverses direction.
Only the current lead receives a private notice and uses the same public interaction flow as every other player.
Market weight and track position are distinct testable semantics even when driven by the same order.
Clicking a normal card in the viewer's segment directly attempts its cash purchase.
A purchased normal card enters personal discard and cannot be used immediately.
Ordinary-card price has no automatic region, monster, sunlight, or GDP modifier.
Each player owns a personal draw pile, normal hand, committed escrow, and discard pile.
Played normal cards cycle through escrow and resolution into discard rather than disappearing.
Personal deck shuffle and reshuffle are authoritative, persisted, and replayable.
The starter deck contains one level-I factory and one level-I market for each of six colors.
The authoritative RNG shuffles twelve starter cards and deals five at random.
The opening hand is not altered to force an economic combination.
Initial assets or an explicit setup exemption must prevent a zero-economy deadlock without changing the random hand.
The normal hand has an absolute five slots with no capacity modifier and is independent from commodity inventory.
Normal cards are not replenished or reshuffled during submission or resolution.
Hand refill and optional merge decisions occur only in the between-batch maintenance phase.
Normal-card merge is always an optional player decision.
Only equivalent unlocked cards in the same player's normal hand can merge.
Normal-card merging uses equal-level pairs and ends at level IV.
A merge is free but produces an authoritative receipt and a new card instance identity.
Commodity cards use an independent five-slot inventory.
Clicking a commodity card in the viewer's segment directly attempts its claim.
Commodity merge is an optional player decision.
Commodity levels are linear base units and stop at level III.
Only matching unlocked commodities owned by the same player can merge.
Monster and military sources may grant actions that remain bound to their source and outside both card inventories.
An active bound action consumes one batch action slot while a passive ability does not.
Each submission window lasts thirty seconds and locks one batch.
A new window opens only after resolution, asset refresh, and hand maintenance are complete.
All active action kinds share a maximum of five actions per player per batch.
Every action has complete prebound targets, local order, and visible cost before queue lock.
Cards, targets, and local order are immutable after lock.
A local queue locks only if all of its actions can reserve their full six-color costs atomically.
Each action consumes or releases only its own reservation according to its authoritative result.
Assets expected from the next refresh cannot fund the current batch.
The player-facing resource is six-color assets, not mana.
Each color has an independent asset cap of six.
Assets top up at the cycle boundary rather than recovering continuously.
Queue lock freezes the player's own completed per-color GDP snapshot used for the later refresh.
The frozen snapshot is applied once after the entire batch resolves and reservations settle.
Unused assets persist, cap overflow is discarded, and fixed-point remainder preserves small accrual.
Only the player's own same-color GDP refreshes that player's assets, and GDP never drives track supply.
Every active action declares a complete six-color asset cost in authoritative data.
Any-asset cost is a payment constraint over six colors, not a seventh asset pool.
V0.7 has no interactive counter window or counter stack.
Resolution accepts no new gameplay input or target selection.
Defense resolves from precommitted actions or automatic state without opening an input window.
Global resolution rotates by local action index through the frozen hidden lead order.
The public queue reveals allowed action facts but no actor identity or owner-specific cue.
World simulation continues during the thirty-second submission window.
World simulation pauses while cards resolve sequentially.
No ordinary world tick is inserted between resolving cards.
Sunlight affects declared facility work-rate channels only.
Sunlit facilities operate at 200 percent and dark facilities at 100 percent.
Only explicitly declared work-rate channels receive the solar multiplier.
Solar state comes from Core and does not alter cards, capacity, stock, combat power, or construction facts.
V0.7 initially inherits every unmodified V0.6 end condition and comparison, but all triggers enter the same pending macro-round gate.
Final settlement is gated by completed batch maintenance and a complete lead macro round.
The boundary revalidates victory; failure resumes play and success enters exact-once final settlement.
This frozen target does not change runtime and future production ownership must cut over atomically without dual writers.
Lead and color-cycle cursors advance independently from one authoritative completed-card-batch receipt.
An AI seat receives only the same self-owned private lead fact that a human seat legally owns.
A replacement track card remains locked until the next authoritative scroll sequence.
A normal-card merge may not reduce all owned normal-card instances below five.
The initial unified-track supply emits only level-one normal and commodity cards.
A claimed commodity is usable in the current batch only when the local queue is still unlocked.
Every action closes invalid-target resolution; the default fully refunds reserved assets and discards the card.
Lead identity is never directly published, while inference from lawful public outcomes remains possible.

inherited_v06_rules.statement: The supported PVE roster remains three through eight players.
Alien role selection remains public and non-duplicated.
Starter monster identity remains independent from role identity and summoning remains voluntary.
Monsters continue to auto-act from authoritative behavior rules.
Facility legal-region semantics remain the initial V0.7 basis except where this constitution changes sunlight effects.
Unmodified route and transport semantics remain the initial basis.
Cash and GDP retain their existing economic meaning except for the explicitly changed asset and track relationships.
Existing victory qualification and audit comparison are inherited behind the new macro-round gate.
Rules in untouched domains remain the initial basis until explicitly amended.
The existing anonymous-play information boundary is inherited and strengthened by owner-anonymous resolution.
